recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It preserves the previously published email subject rule using the current Subscription.parameter model and avoids broader changes to generic parameter semantics or generated artifacts.
issue_request: FHIR-14642 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and asked to document that when Subscription.channel.type is email, Subscription.channel.header sets the email subject.
initial_application: The request was applied in SVN revision 13401, mirrored as git commit 73cab4d6f35939116870402fb00b3717d6177a2f, which added narrative saying Subscription.channel.header sets the email subject. Later Subscription redesign commits rewrote the channel narrative and the exact sentence disappeared.
additional_context: Subscription remains active in the current build. R5 redesign work flattened Subscription.channel and FHIR-39034 replaced the old string-valued Subscription.header with key/value Subscription.parameter. FHIR-21286 refined email body and attachment behavior but did not reverse the email subject rule. Community searches found no Zulip or Confluence decision contradicting the Jira/source-history conclusion.
reconciliation: Updated source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml in the Email channel section to state that, when present, a Subscription.parameter with name Subject sets the email notification subject line to the supplied value.
source_changes: source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml: added a narrow Email channel paragraph documenting Subscription.parameter.name = Subject as the email subject-line value.
